video_title: Stephen A. says ‘IT’S NOW OR NEVER’ for the NY Knicks to win an NBA Championship! | First Take

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: The New York Knicks have not been to the NBA Finals in 27 years
quotes.excerpt: You the New York Knicks, you haven't been to the NBA Finals in 27 years.
quotes.quote: It is now or never, y'all. Let me tell you something. You the New York Knicks, you haven't been to the NBA Finals in 27 years. My hairline was two feet forward, Michael Wilbon had hair, you understand? Monica was a toddler for crying out loud. So were you, Jay. Here is the bottom line: when you look at the New York Knicks, it is 27 years since you've been to the Finals. It is 32 years since you were relevant enough to be considered a team that could win the championship.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith and Jay Williams debate if the Knicks can win now
quotes.excerpt: If they lose, are you going to say never again I don't want the next year?

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Williams
text_blocks.text: So if they lose, are you going to say never again I don't want the next year? I don't want to be back?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: That is what now or never means. Come on now. You and I major in the use of the language.

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Williams
text_blocks.text: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has got a team that has got 13 first-round picks and 16 second-round picks through 2032. Where are they going, Stephen A.?

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Monica McNutt argues the Knicks must cherish the moment in the Finals
quotes.excerpt: You just have to cherish the moment.

text_blocks.speaker: Monica McNutt
text_blocks.text: It is now for both teams. You need to make take advantage of the present because you don't know. It is no guarantee. Victor Wembanyama, we are looking and it looks different in terms of their likelihood. But I would say that it is now for the Knicks for sure. You just have to cherish the moment.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: I think this question derives from the fact of the path, who they had to play to get here, the health. They have had so much rest. When are we going to see this again? This is like historic.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith accuses Jay Williams of not being sensitive to his suffering
quotes.excerpt: She accuses me of not being sensitive enough to her suffering, and that is what I am accusing you of.
quotes.quote: She accuses me of not being sensitive enough to her suffering, and that is what I am accusing you of. You are not being sensitive enough to the suffering. And you, I don't even want to get started with you. You brag about Chicago all the time, Jay. You are ridiculous. The suffering matters.

quotes.speaker: Jay Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Williams reflects on covering Patrick Ewing and the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I spent more time in New York for the Washington Post covering Patrick Ewing.
quotes.quote: As you know, I did the very first interview that Patrick Ewing ever did at Georgetown. I spent more time in New York for the Washington Post covering Patrick Ewing, who for those four years was ours, right? I spent all that time covering Patrick. There are people in the Knicks organization starting with Patrick Ewing that I root for. I was there for all of court-side, for all of Patrick's suffering. So when I look at these Knicks, if there is one person that I think of that I'd like to see them win for him, it is Patrick Ewing.
